briefs.rationale: The rewritten brief keeps the differentiability/Cauchy-Riemann and power-series strands and covers the gained coordinate-and-path-transport page: the real-linear coordinate identification C = R^2 as a bijective isometry carrying affine segments and topology, the transport of real total differentiability, and complex path length defined polygonally, equal to the Euclidean coordinate length, finite exactly for bounded-variation real and imaginary parts, given by the piecewise-C^1 speed integral and invariant under monotone surjective reparametrization. Only the section body changed; the sync's single frontmatter insertion was correct and the page order is preserved, so no mechanical repair was needed.

The rewritten brief keeps the Banach-space, Fourier, Hahn--Banach/duality, Hilbert, operator, Banach-algebra, Gelfand, spectral, calculus and direct-integral strands with their DC and AC_omega boundaries, and covers the two gained pages: complex norms with absolute homogeneity under every complex scalar, realification preserving the norm and induced metric, coordinate sum norms on C^n including the zero space, restricted norms on complex subspaces, equivalent complex norms with positive real constants; and the realified-subspace page, where a complex normed subspace becomes a real normed subspace with the restricted metric and a supplied finite complex basis interleaves to a real basis, zero dimension included. The sync's two frontmatter insertions were correct; no mechanical repair was needed.

The rewritten brief keeps the measure, integration, Lp, representation, differentiation, Hausdorff, complex-Lp, interpolation and FTC strands with their choice and sigma-finiteness hypotheses, the mixing criteria and the dynamics through the maximal ergodic inequality and the Birkhoff and von Neumann theorems, and covers the gained pointwise-extended-real-product page: a total pointwise product of extended-real functions with the zero rule on every ordered zero-infinity pair, sign rules for infinite factors and no measurability claim. The sync's frontmatter insertion was correct; no mechanical repair was needed.
